I was raised to be polite, and I know how rude it is to cut people off. I hate when people do it to me. But, despite knowing all of that, and despite genuinely trying to be a good listener... yes. It’s like... okay, so picture this. My husband will be telling a story, right? Maybe he’s talking about something that happened at work, or he’s on the phone with his sister, and he’ll pause for just a half-second to take a breath or find a word. And my brain just... fills in the blank. And before I even have the conscious thought of, "Oh, I should wait my turn," the words are already out of my mouth. I’ll just jump right into his conversation, or I’ll finish his sentence for him, or I’ll completely derail his point because a thought popped into my head and it just *had* to come out right that exact second. 

It’s not like I’m sitting there thinking, "What I have to say is more important than what he’s saying." It’s not malicious at all. It’s just... the response just bursts out of me before I’ve managed to put the brakes on and make myself wait. It’s like there’s no filter between the thought forming in my brain and my mouth opening to say it. 

Just the other day, we had some neighbors over for coffee—just a casual thing on the patio—and the husband was explaining this whole complicated issue they were having with their landscaping contractor. And I swear, I interrupted him at least four times. I’d be like, "Oh, did you try calling this other guy?" or "Wait, didn't they say they were going to use the blue stone instead of the pavers?" And every time I did it, I could see my husband giving me that *look* out of the corner of his eye. You know the look. The "please let him finish his story" look. And in the moment, I’d realize what I did, and I’d feel terrible, and I’d apologize and say, "I’m so sorry, please go on," but then three minutes later, I’d do it again! It’s just so incredibly frustrating because I know better, but it’s like my mouth is moving faster than my self-control.

I work as a wholesale and retail buyer, and I’ve been doing this since I finished high school, so I know my job, I know how the inventory works, and I know how to spot when something is off. It’s like they’re all secretly tracking my buys. He spent like an hour showing me how the reports don't prove that anyone is messing with my numbers, but I just... I know what I see. I know they're tracking me. Even when he shows me that paperwork, it doesn't explain how the vendors know exactly when to shift the numbers to make my buys look like a total failure.
